source.title: Variants of RMSProp and Adagrad with Logarithmic Regret Bounds

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some experimental results are shown only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers on held-out test accuracy in deep-learning experiments, using a different setup from the optimizer-generalization claim. It reports outcomes for V4 but does not test the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's results bear on V4 through test-accuracy comparisons. Its strongly convex regret and training-objective results do not measure the training-to-test generalization gap. Specific test-accuracy values are presented in figures; the text gives only qualitative summaries. Cited optimizer comparisons are not recorded as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on image-classification test accuracy under learning-rate-only tuning, directly bearing on V4. Its convex regret bounds and training-objective comparisons alone do not test held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present convergence analysis for RMSProp and logarithmic regret bounds for SC-Adagrad and SC-RMSProp, report strong empirical performance including deep-network test accuracy, and leave unexplained why methods designed for strongly convex problems work well in deep learning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares SGD, Adam, Adagrad, RMSProp, RMSProp (Ours), SC-RMSProp and SC-Adagrad on image classification, selecting each optimizer's learning rate for best test performance after a fixed number of epochs. It does not reproduce the cited optimizer studies' benchmarks or tuning protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparative outcomes vary by architecture and dataset. Hyperparameter tuning is limited to learning rate; the selected rate is optimized separately for best test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical regret bounds and empirical regret or training-objective improvements for strongly convex optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed adaptive variants improve optimization guarantees and performance on strongly convex problems.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70, 2017
record.problems: Test-accuracy numbers are shown in figures without numeric values stated in the text. The comparison tunes only the learning rate over a small stated set; no uncertainty estimates are reported. Results are on image datasets and do not measure the train-test gap directly.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible test-accuracy findings with explicit textual outcomes were left out. Figures also show optimizer curves, but exact figure-only values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.

No explicit comparative conclusion about convolutional versus fully connected generalization or local connectivity; the supplied figure text does not preserve the accuracy curves needed for a reliable architecture comparison.

Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; momentum-SGD comparisons. Training and test objectives use separately selected learning rates, so their reported rankings do not establish paired training-versus-test behavior for the same fitted models.
Dropout is used but its effect is not isolated.

record.verdict_notes: R2 and R3 justify no verdict without readable comparisons with SGD. The original supports label mistakes any optimizer difference for the directional claim in V4. Exact figure-only comparisons were already declared omitted in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; equal or better training performance paired with worse held-out performance; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language-model results.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
